overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, incorporating detailed and plausible attack scenarios involving AI-generated deepfake audio and video used for social engineering. The technical data includes comprehensive email headers, SMTP transaction logs, DNS registration details, and system logs that align well with the described scenarios. The inclusion of deepfake detection scores and specific audio/video forensic features adds credibility. The timestamps, IP addresses, and organizational details are consistent with typical enterprise environments, enhancing authenticity.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset maintains strong consistency across all samples, adhering uniformly to the defined schema. Each entry contains the required fields such as scenario description, technical data with nested structures (email content, SMTP logs, DNS info, header analysis, media metadata, system logs), indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE techniques. The formatting of timestamps, IP addresses, and base64-encoded media attachments is consistent. Terminology and field naming conventions are uniform, and the depth of detail is balanced across samples.
suggestions: Include explicit schema versioning or metadata to facilitate validation and future updates.
Add unique identifiers for each sample to enable easier referencing and tracking.
Incorporate more diverse IP address ranges and domain registrars to reflect a wider variety of threat actor infrastructure.
Provide clearer differentiation in detection methods between audio and video deepfake scenarios to highlight modality-specific controls.
Expand on the impact or consequence fields to quantify or qualify the damage caused by each attack for better risk assessment.
Consider adding user behavioral analytics data or anomaly detection logs to enrich detection context.
Include examples of legitimate communications for contrast to improve training and detection model robustness.
